narrative:
The model estimates a 70% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

Your relatively short overall work experience of 1-5 years was the strongest factor pulling the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expected to stay, only about half had similarly limited experience, while the rest had six or more years. This limited tenure signals higher turnover risk to the system.

The second most influential factor was that you have received other job offers while working here. Having external opportunities strongly pushed the prediction toward you eventually leaving, as it suggests you have realistic alternatives available.

Third, the fact that you are not experiencing psychological exhaustion worked in your favor and pulled the prediction slightly back toward staying. Most employees the model sees as likely to remain also report low mental fatigue, so this is a positive element in your profile.

Taken together, your early-career stage and the presence of outside offers outweighed the protective effect of good mental health, leading to the 70% probability of departure. The organization should discuss your career goals and explore whether clearer advancement paths could be created to retain you. You may want to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your longer-term plans.
